messages.content: what is artificial intelligence?
artificial intelligence is software that can learn patterns and make useful predictions or responses.
what is machine learning?
machine learning is a way for computers to learn from examples instead of fixed rules.
what is deep learning?
deep learning uses neural networks with many layers to learn complex patterns.
what is a neural network?
a neural network is a model made of connected layers that transform input into output.
what is a token?
a token is a small unit of text that a language model processes.
what is a tokenizer?
a tokenizer converts text into token ids that a model can understand.
what is a vocabulary?
a vocabulary is the set of tokens known by the tokenizer and model.
what is an embedding?
an embedding is a vector representation of a token.
what is attention?
attention lets a model focus on important previous tokens when making a prediction.
what is causal attention?
causal attention prevents the model from looking at future tokens during training.
what is a transformer?
a transformer is a neural network architecture based on attention and feed-forward layers.
what is a language model?
a language model predicts the next token based on previous tokens.
what is pretraining?
pretraining teaches a model general language patterns from a large text dataset.
what is fine tuning?
fine tuning adapts a trained model to a specific task or style.
what is loss?
loss measures how far the model prediction is from the correct target.
why should loss go down?
lower loss usually means the model is getting better at predicting training examples.
what is overfitting?
overfitting happens when a model memorizes training data and performs poorly on new data.
how can we reduce overfitting?
use more data, validation checks, dropout, regularization, and avoid training too long.
what is validation loss?
validation loss measures model performance on data not used directly for training.
what is a checkpoint?
a checkpoint is a saved copy of model weights and settings.
why save tokenizer with model?
the model depends on the tokenizer vocabulary, so they must be reused together.
what is batch size?
batch size is the number of training samples processed at once.
what is learning rate?
learning rate controls how large each model update is during training.
what is an epoch?
an epoch is one full pass through the training dataset.
why does this project use iterations?
it samples random batches, so training duration is controlled by max iterations.
how can we improve this chatbot?
add cleaner data, train longer, tune the model size, and evaluate responses carefully.
why are responses bad at first?
the model starts with random weights and needs many examples to learn useful patterns.
can a small model chat like a human?
a small model can learn simple patterns, but human-like chat needs much more data and compute.
should i train from scratch or fine tune?
train from scratch for learning, but fine tune a pretrained model for better real-world quality.
what is inference?
inference is using a trained model to generate predictions or responses.
